Trump Should Just Admit He Screwed Up… The Iran war was obviously a mistake. Why not say so?
￼
By Stephen Walt @ForeignPolicy
foreignpolicy.com/2026/05/28…

I joined @democracynow with Amy Goodman and Juan González to discuss the U.S.-Iran peace talks, the shaky ceasefire, and the path toward ending the war on Iran.

VIDEO: piped.video/KQCbBN_tBMk?si=pRNy…

I told @BBCWorld that the U.S. and Iran are very close to a peace deal. Main points are: permanent end to the regional war, mutual reopening of Hormuz, economic relief for Iran, and eventually a nuclear agreement.

The challenge is trust. There is very little of it on either side, which means diplomacy could unravel at any moment.

Video

What will Iran do with the Strait of Hormuz?

I told @Channel4News there’s active debate in Iran over how the Strait should be managed moving forward, in both war and peace.

Watch the full episode:

Spoke to @TheHill about U.S.-Iran peace talks and the battle of narratives. 

“We know he cares about the media coverage, we know he cares about criticism,” Negar Mortazavi told this column. “The criticism is factual when people say he is not winning. I think that is correct.”

Mortazavi contended that, in terms of public perception, both Iran and the U.S. would have to live with some measure of compromise. “There needs to be an understanding from both sides that there will be no absolute winner

Sky News (@SkyNews)

Who fired the tomahawk missile at the school in Minab? @Stone_SkyNews asked the US Admiral in charge of the war.

It's after Sky News reported from the Iranian city where more than 150 people, including 120 children, were killed in a strike on the first day of the war.

Trump’s Iran war doom loop:
Escalate, retreat, repeat 
piped.video/LYA2s2gM4Qo?si=-xkE…

Trump’s Iran War Doom Loop:
Escalate, Retreat, Repeat 

I joined @Aljazeera Listening Post to discuss how American media has long helped dehumanize the enemy and manufacture consent for wars.
(Watch the full show below)

Video

Spoke to @BBCWorld about the possibility of a U.S.-Iran peace deal, what it means for Lebanon and the rest of the region, and how Tehran and Washington can meet somewhere mid way.

Video

Indeed. Most of the world didn’t know where the Strait of Hormuz was until the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in two wars that led to a global crisis and now the entire world wants the Strait to reopen.


Joe Kent (@joekent16jan19)

Iran would have no incentive to mine the Strait of Hormuz if we weren’t there. 

Pull our forces out & Iran faces major pressure to open the Strait from the rest of the world & loses their justification. 

Staying in our current posture is inviting escalation

LATEST:

I’m hearing from sources on all sides that US–Iran peace deal is near the finish line. There has been real progress and serious movement from both Tehran and Washington. That’s why war hawks are now making a last-minute push to torpedo it.

Pakistan, Qatar, Oman, Turkey, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and others have spent months trying to end a war that devastated the region and threatened global stability.

Across the Middle East, civilians want peace, not more forever wars.
